atoms.b: My brother hurt ((himself --hisself)) pretty badly during the game. I noticed how he twisted his ankle abruptly. It looked so bad, I could almost feel the pain ((myself --mine)). Afterwards, my friends and I hurried to the bench to see how he was doing. His teammates were standing at the entrance and appreciated our help, but let us know that the team could take care of ((themselves --themselfs)).

atoms.b: Axolotls are a type of salamander and have unique needs. I would not be able to take care of our axolotls ((myself --ourselves)), which is why I am thankful for my sister’s help. Apart from the proper habitat for our axolotls, my sister and I even made some of the aquarium’s decoration ((ourselves --yourselves)). Axolotls should not be kept with fish, because they may decide to find dinner ((themselves --ourselves)) instead of waiting for their owners to feed them. Trust me, my sister, Claire, found this out ((--himself herself)) when she came home from work and was unable to find our fish...

instruction.text: Which definition for reflexive pronouns is correct?

hint.text:
For example:
I did this by myself.
→ myself = reflexive pronoun
hint.sound: For example: I did this by myself. Myself is a reflexive pronoun
hint.label: Example

b: ++Reflexive pronouns are words that refer back to the person or thing doing the action.
Reflexive pronouns are words that can replace the verb of a sentence.
Reflexive pronouns are words that don’t name or refer to any specific thing or person.
